newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Davids seeks ACCC action on Woolworths.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Davids seeks ACCC action on Woolworths.

text.p: Grocery wholesaler Davids Ltd said on Tuesday it has asked the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission to force Woolworths Ltd to divest some of its Cannons stores in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT).
Chairman John David told a media briefing the submission was made this week on the basis of market share.
Davids had not yet had a response from the ACCC, Australia's anti-monopoly authority.
"We have asked for possible divestiture of some of the stores," David said.
Woolworths last year purchased 11 independent Cannons supermarkets in the ACT and New South Wales, as well as wholesaler Australian Independent Wholesalers Pty Ltd (AIW).
The ACCC said it had no objection to the purchase.
However, the purchase had given Woolworths more than 80 percent of the large "Valley" segment of the ACT retail market, and more than 70 percent of the total Canberra market, David said.
"I find it a little hard to justify that you would permit that takeover with that sort of market size and market dominance," he said.
David also questioned Woolworths' plans to expand the operations of AIW into other states.
"We wonder what their objectives are," he said.
David said he could not understand the commercial logic of Woolworths moving into the wholesale market.
"Maybe the logic is that they simply want to disrupt us and disrupt independents, soften our underbelly ... to a degree that perhaps they can take a bigger market share," he said.
Woolworths said last month it had decided to expand AIW following approaches to the company by independent supermarkets and after researching the market.
David said he had seen contracts which Woolworths was offering to independent retail stores, and did not believe the new competition would lead to a discounting war.
